chapter: Early memories on St. Philip Street
title: Bill Russell's visit to the St. Philip Street house
summary: Bill Russell and other musicians visited, he left money with her mother, and the Burgundy Street Blues was recorded in the backyard. Russell and Bunk Johnson teased her into eating, and Russell still sends a Christmas card with $5.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Do you remember that time? That would be about right. That's when my now and Jeffries met Bill Russell. Yeah. He and a couple of other guys, I don't know their name offhand, came to the house and, um, he didn't believe in banks. He asked my mother to keep his money for him. A lot of them spent the night on the floor. And I understand that was when they made the recording of the Bundy Street Blues in the backyard. And then, um, Lawrence. Who? Lawrence. Yeah, and Uncle Lawrence to me. And, um, Slow Drake, Mr. Jim Robinson. I don't know if he was playing drum at the time. Well, what do you, how do you remember Bill Russell at that time? Well, I was one who didn't care to eat very much.
And, um, he and Ron Johnson used to kid me a lot.

And Lisa was one who didn't care to eat very much. And, um, he and Ron Johnson used to kid me a lot. At least, Ron did anyway, about eating my food all the time. Every time my mother would fix it, I wouldn't eat it. And he'd say, well, he was going to eat my food. So, between the two of them, they coaxed me into eating. And, um, I don't know, I just more or less took to Bill Russell. And from that time on up until now, every Christmas, he sends me my Christmas card with a $5 bill in it. And, I don't know, I just liked it, and I just took to him from a child.
